tools.name: schedule_add
tools.title: Schedule for later
tools.description: Leaves something to happen later, once, on this computer, as `nightdrive schedule` does: at a time of day, in so many minutes (up to a week), at the first unlock after the computer next wakes from sleep (wake), or at the next login. Use it to carry on later by yourself: when the user says to go on in the morning, schedule a message to Claude for wake (or a time), saying what to do and where the work stands, to this session (to: its name or id from sessions_list) or to a new session. A text whose first word is a program (or nightdrive) runs as a shell command, any other is a message to Claude; as says which instead. The user always allows it on Nightdrive's card first, and the list and its notifications show it as by Claude. Nothing runs behind the lock: a time that passes while the computer sleeps runs at the unlock. Returns the row as schedule_list gives it. For a reminder banner, a reminder is better.

when.title: When
when.description: Minutes from now (15, 90m, 1h30m; up to a week), a time of day (07:30: the next one, tomorrow's once today's has passed), wake (the first unlock after the computer next wakes from sleep) or login (the next login)

text.title: What
text.description: A shell command line (make && notify-send done), or a message to Claude: what to do then, whole, as the session will read it with nothing else to go on

as.title: As
as.description: run: a shell command; claude: a message to Claude. Without it, read from the text's first word

to.title: To session
to.description: For a message: the Claude Code session that gets it (its id, or its name as sessions_list gives it); it is typed into its window if it runs, else resumed with it. Without it a new session gets the message. Not with as: run

tools.name: schedule_list
tools.title: Scheduled for later
tools.description: What waits in `nightdrive schedule` (schedule_add's and the user's own), by time, then wake and login: {commands: [{id, when (time, wake or login), label, at (ISO 8601), at_unix, clock (HH:MM), minutes_left, state (waiting; unlock: its time came under the lock; missed: asks Run or Skip; due), kind (run or claude), to (the session a message is for), command (the line or the message), by (user or claude)}]}.

tools.name: schedule_cancel
tools.title: Cancel a scheduled one
tools.description: Takes one that waits in `nightdrive schedule` away before it runs, by its id from schedule_list. Undo gives it back as it was, unless its time has passed meanwhile.
